column1: # Modal-framework frames index. Tab-separated; `#` lines are comments.
# GENERATED — do not edit. Every row is derived from the `Modal Framework` pantry group, so the
# index cannot drift from the frames the way a hand-kept list did (see
# `views::modal_framework::index` for the failure that motivated it).
#   PNG (all of them):  cargo run -p wqm-tui --features png-capture,tui-pantry \
#   grid / ANSI (one):  cargo pantry dump "Modal Framework" --variant "<variant>" \
#   browse:             cargo pantry          (Views tab, group "Modal Framework")
# Both instruments render the SAME pantry variant, so they cannot disagree about what was
# drawn. Judge COLOUR from the PNG and GLYPHS/ATTRIBUTES from the grid — png-capture drops
# the `●` radio glyph (wqm#283), U+E0B0 is invisible in most text views, and no still image
# The theme is Catppuccin Mocha unless the variant says otherwise.

column4: what it shows

The floor, derived: border + the four top rows + the three bottom ones + ONE content row. One row less and the viewport is empty
Below the floor there is no window, so the message is not drawn in one. It names the size needed AND the size present, and shortens rather than truncating
Item 1's first half: a Configuration-like window is as tall as what it holds, capped by the maximum

PROPOSED. The same hue at the same strength, with L* left where the rung put it: 13 of 15 themes clear the floor, and the two that fail fail untinted too
The adversarial theme: the thinnest ladder of the fifteen, and the one where round 1's SET fill fell below a just-noticeable difference
A light theme, where the ladder runs the other way — the case a design measured only on Mocha cannot see

column3: 09 fields — view mode, black on the cursor row
column4: The selected field takes the table's own block and its text goes black bold, which ruling 7 already gave it

column3: 10 fields — tick box, the two states side by side
column4: Space toggles it, and the mark is a SHAPE — `[✓] yes` against `[ ] no` — so the state survives a terminal that refuses colour (r06 #8)
PROPOSED. The underline gone, the SET carried by the fill, and the ACTIVE field derived light enough to carry black text
PROPOSED. The underline gone, the SET carried by the fill, and the ACTIVE field derived light enough to carry black text
The active button BOLD and the rest normal; h/l or left/right move within the field

column3: 13 fields — the same radio as a column (B)
column4: The whole column takes the highlight, one choice per row, and j/k move within it
Item 3: the frame gone, every other field's highlight gone, the current value first and the rest sorted under it
`ts` typed: the list narrows by subsequence, and the cursor is on the best match rather than on a value that may no longer be in the list

column3: 16 fields — single line, vim INSERT (bar, blinking)
column4: The caret is a bar carrying the real SLOW_BLINK attribute. Judge it from a cell dump — a PNG cannot show an attribute and should not be asked to

column3: 17 fields — single line, vim NORMAL (block, steady)
column4: A block ON a character, and the ONE caret that does not blink — which is the only thing separating it from visual's
EMACS style: the terminal owns the cursor, so nothing is painted. A still frame has no terminal, which is why this one shows no caret at all
The fill IS the box: a multi-line field's frame is the extent of its background, so no border is drawn around it
PROPOSED. No hue spent: the selected-row tint at a second scale, with whichever text end is legible on it
A real colour, as asked — and on every non-Catppuccin theme it IS the data cursor's hue, so the selection and the row cursor share one

column3: 22 fields — the same edit, driven by real keystrokes
column4: Not constructed in the state a keystroke would produce — `jjjjjj e A 0` through Stack::key, so the frame is evidence the live editor is wired in and not only that the renderer works
PROPOSED. Item 4: the column is informational and does not need its own region — the text stands on the window like everything else
Item 4: *the headers are optional*. With none, the row the header occupied goes back to data
A trail of one is all current: no ancestor run, and the segment opens straight off the window
One ancestor and the current crumb, with the transition between them
PROPOSED. Two ancestors sharing one run of full-saturation accent, the separator drawn INSIDE it, then the current crumb on a lighter run
What it replaces: *not visible enough* — muted text and a faint chevron, spending no background at all

column3: 29 banner — view vs edit, no `-- EDIT --`
column4: Item (b): the columnar change IS the indication, so the banner is gone. This is edit mode, and nothing on the title row says so

column3: 30 confirm — a window quietened under its own guard
column4: Item (c): the window beneath gets the SAME treatment the page gets — the existing ModalScope, one level deeper, rather than a second rule meaning the same thing

column3: 32 edge — spacing only (the default, shown alone)
column4: PROPOSED. Item (e): the same rect, fill and padding with no glyphs — the content does not move by a column, so the pair differs in ink alone

column3: 33 degradation — the SET mark under NO_COLOR
column4: The ladder collapses onto four slots, so the fill cannot carry the SET — and the underline comes back, only here

column3: 34 degradation — the same frame at ansi16
column4: Sixteen slots: the trail keeps its glyphs and loses its hue separation, which is what item (a) costs on a poor terminal
The same record part-way down: the thumb is off both ends and the DEFAULT header has not scrolled away with the data
No fields at all: the word the table already uses, and no header over a column with nothing in it
The Queue's own ListPane, pre-filtered to the library it was drilled in from, with the fifth row naming that floor
A floor that matches nothing: the column titles stay, because that row IS the view
Before the push: the record, whole. Only the viewport moves — the decoration is the window's and is already at its destination
Half-way: the record leaving left, the queue arriving from the right. The only frame that says whether the motion will read
After the push: the queue, whole, under the trail it arrived with
Backspace over a dirty view: the existing modal on Layer2, centred on the WINDOW because a dialogue belongs to what it asks about
The help window IS this framework: a container and a fixed scrollable content — and the content does not fit, which is the scroll the ruling asks for
Every row repeating `open-books` in its widest fixed column — twenty columns carrying no information
The caller's other choice, and the usual one: a drilled-in view drops the column it was pinned by, and Object gets the width
